standard_prerequisites.name: A morphism of algebraic spaces is an isomorphism exactly when it is so on stalks at geometric points
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Properties of Spaces, theorem spaces-properties-theorem-exactness-stalks (invoked at proof line 578)
standard_prerequisites.use: It reduces the verification of the isomorphism of module sheaves to the corresponding statement about stalks at geometric points.

standard_prerequisites.name: The behaviour of stalks under pullback and under pushforward along a finite morphism
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Properties of Spaces, label spaces-properties-lemma-stalk-pullback (invoked at proof line 600) and Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, label lemma-stalk-push-finite (invoked at proof line 602)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first describes the stalks of $f^*\mathcal{G}$, the second identifies the stalk of a pushforward along a finite morphism with the product of the stalks over the finitely many geometric lifts.

standard_prerequisites.name: Tensor products commute with taking stalks
standard_prerequisites.use: It allows the two sides of the displayed identity of stalks to be rewritten as tensor products over the residue field rings, where the equality is formal.

core_obligations: Identify the canonical map of the statement as the map adjoint to the natural map $f^*\mathcal{G} \otimes_\mathcal{A} f^*f_*\mathcal{F} \to f^*\mathcal{G} \otimes_\mathcal{A} \mathcal{F}$ built from the identity and the adjunction (proof lines 567-576).
Reduce the claim to a statement about stalks at geometric points of $Y$ (proof lines 577-580).

Compute both sides at a geometric point with lifts $\overline{x}_1, \ldots, \overline{x}_n$: the stalk of the pushforward is the direct sum of the stalks of $\mathcal{F}$ over the lifts, so the asserted identity becomes the distributivity of the tensor product over that direct sum (proof lines 580-596).
Conclude with the compatibility of tensor products with stalks, the pullback stalk description and the finite pushforward stalk computation (proof lines 597-602).
proof_roadmap: The adjoint description of the map (proof lines 567-576).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the projection formula for a finite morphism of algebraic spaces carrying sheaves of rings: the canonical map comparing the tensor product with the pushforward of the tensor product is an isomorphism (statement lines 542-564). The proof writes the map as an adjoint, reduces to stalks at geometric points, identifies the stalk of the pushforward as a finite direct sum over the lifts of the point and checks the resulting distributive identity, using the pullback and pushforward stalk descriptions. The stalk computation is the substance, so the claim is H2.
